speak.tip.TWO_POINTERS: I notice the input is sorted or can be sorted. I will place two pointers and move the one that improves the invariant, achieving linear time after sorting.
speak.tip.SLIDING_WINDOW: This asks for a contiguous subarray/substring with a constraint. I will expand the right bound, shrink the left when invalid, and track the best window.
speak.tip.FAST_SLOW_POINTERS: I will use a slow pointer stepping once and a fast pointer stepping twice to detect a cycle or find the middle in constant space.
speak.tip.TREE_DFS: I will recurse on the tree, defining what each call returns, handling the null base case, then combining left and right results.
speak.tip.TREE_BFS: I will process nodes level by level with a queue; the queue size at the start of each loop is the width of the current level.
speak.tip.DYNAMIC_PROGRAMMING: I will define the state, the recurrence, and base cases, then fill bottom-up to avoid recomputing overlapping subproblems.
speak.tip.GRAPHS: I will model this as a graph, choose BFS or DFS, and track visited nodes to explore connectivity or shortest paths.
speak.tip.BACKTRACKING: I will build a partial solution, prune when constraints fail, then undo the choice and try the next option.
speak.tip.INTERVALS: I will sort intervals by start, then merge or scan overlaps in a single pass while tracking the active end.
speak.tip.TOP_K_ELEMENTS: I will keep a heap of size K so each insertion stays logarithmic in K, giving an efficient top-K selection.
speak.tip.MODIFIED_BINARY_SEARCH: I will binary search on a rotated or unbounded range, deciding which half is still sorted or still feasible each step.
speak.tip.DEFAULT: I will restate the problem, identify the pattern, state time and space complexity, then walk through a small example before coding.
diagram.caption.TWO_POINTERS: L and R move toward the goal — each step discards impossible pairs.
diagram.caption.SLIDING_WINDOW: Expand right to include; shrink left when the constraint breaks.
diagram.caption.TREE_DFS: Go deep along a branch, then backtrack — preorder / inorder / postorder.
diagram.caption.TREE_BFS: Queue processes the tree level by level.
diagram.caption.FAST_SLOW_POINTERS: Fast moves 2×; if they meet, a cycle exists.
diagram.caption.INTERVALS: Sort by start, then merge when the next start overlaps the current end.
diagram.caption.TOP_K_ELEMENTS: Keep a bounded heap of size K; push/pop to retain only the best K.
diagram.caption.MODIFIED_BINARY_SEARCH: Decide which half is sorted or feasible, then discard the other half.
diagram.caption.BACKTRACKING: Try a choice, recurse, then undo and try the next option.

judge.tip.title: Failure insight
judge.tip.wrong: Wrong answer — re-check invariants, off-by-one bounds, and how you update state each step.
judge.tip.timeout: Timeout — rethink asymptotic complexity; look for nested loops or repeated work you can cache.
judge.tip.npe: Null pointer — cover null/empty edges and confirm every dereference is guarded.
judge.tip.unsupported: UnsupportedOperation — implement the required method body instead of leaving a stub.
judge.tip.generic: Read the failing case carefully, then bisect your logic against a smaller hand-traced example.

speak.tip.IN_PLACE_LINKED_LIST: I will reverse or reorder links in place with a few pointers, updating next references carefully so no node is lost.
speak.tip.TWO_HEAPS: I will balance a max-heap and a min-heap so the median or boundary stays available in logarithmic time per update.
speak.tip.K_WAY_MERGE: I will merge K sorted streams with a min-heap of size K, always taking the smallest head and advancing that list.
speak.tip.SUBSETS: I will generate subsets or permutations by choosing include-or-skip at each index, or by swapping positions and backtracking.
speak.tip.GREEDY: I will make the locally optimal choice at each step after proving that a greedy choice property holds for this problem.
speak.tip.CYCLIC_SORT: I will place each number at its correct index in a cycle, then scan for the missing or duplicate value.
speak.tip.TOPOLOGICAL_SORT: I will build the graph and indegrees, then Kahn-process zero-indegree nodes until order is complete or a cycle remains.
speak.tip.SORT_AND_SEARCH: I will sort or bucket the input to unlock linear or binary search, trading a sort cost for a simpler scan.
speak.tip.MATRICES: I will treat the matrix as a graph or use boundary/direction indices, careful with visited cells and edges.
speak.tip.STACKS: I will use a stack to track unmatched opens, previous results, or candidates that are no longer useful.
speak.tip.TRIE: I will insert and search strings via a prefix tree, sharing edges so prefix queries stay proportional to word length.
speak.tip.HASH_MAPS: I will store complements or running counts in a hash map so lookups stay expected O(1) while I scan once.
speak.tip.KNOWING_WHAT_TO_TRACK: I will identify the frequency or majority statistic to track, then update counters or Boyer-Moore style votes as I scan.
speak.tip.UNION_FIND: I will union connected components with path compression and rank, answering connectivity in nearly constant time.
speak.tip.CUSTOM_DATA_STRUCTURES: I will combine hash maps with linked structures so get, put, and eviction each stay amortized constant time.
speak.tip.BITWISE: I will use bit masks and XOR properties to pack flags or cancel pairs without extra storage.
speak.tip.MATH_GEOMETRY: I will reduce geometry to slopes, gcd-normalized vectors, or modular arithmetic before scanning points.
speak.tip.SPRING_BOOT_INTERVIEW: I will name the Spring concern—filter, transaction, concurrency, or idempotency—then sketch the failure modes and thread-safety before coding.
